# Getting started with Perplexity for answers that show their sources

> **In short:** Perplexity is an AI-powered search engine. You ask a question in plain language, it searches the web, and each answer includes numbered citations that link to the original sources, so you can check the facts yourself.

By the end of this guide, you'll be able to ask Perplexity a question, read the answer, open the pages it used, and ask a follow-up question. It's a handy habit for research, shopping, or learning something new.

## Before you start

- **A web browser or the Perplexity app.** Go to [perplexity.ai](https://www.perplexity.ai). If it asks you to sign in or create an account, follow the steps on the screen.
- **A question you actually care about.** Real questions make it easier to judge the answer.
- **About 5–10 minutes** the first time.

## Step 1: Open Perplexity

Open [perplexity.ai](https://www.perplexity.ai) in your browser, or open the Perplexity app. Look for the main text box where you type a question. The exact wording and layout can change over time and can differ between the website and the app.

You'll know it worked when you can click or tap into the text box and start typing.

## Step 2: Ask a complete question

Type a full sentence that says exactly what you want to know, then press **Enter** or tap the send button. A complete question works better than a single keyword, because it tells Perplexity what kind of answer you need.

💬 Example: "What are some dog-friendly campgrounds within a two-hour drive of [your city], and what facilities do they have?"

You'll know it worked when an answer appears under your question.

## Step 3: Open the numbered sources

Perplexity's help center says each answer includes numbered citations that link to the original sources. Look for the small numbers next to the facts in the answer, and open one or two of them. Check that the page really says what the answer claims, and look at the date of the page if the topic changes quickly.

You'll know it worked when an original web page opens and you can find the fact from the answer on it.

## Step 4: Check the source labels

Some cited websites carry a small shield icon with a label. According to Perplexity's help center, there are three labels: **Government** (official government websites), **Academic** (scientific sites), and **Trusted** (sites that often appear in results and publish within their area of expertise). Select or hover over a source in the answer to see its label and a one-sentence description.

Keep in mind what Perplexity says about the labels: they describe the type of website, not the accuracy of any single article. No label does not mean a site is low quality, and a label is not an endorsement.

You'll know it worked when you can see a source's label or description, or when you can tell that a source has no label.

## Step 5: Ask a follow-up question

Type your next question in the same conversation. Perplexity's help center says you can ask follow-up questions and it will remember the context of your previous questions, so you don't need to repeat everything.

💬 Example: "Which of those campgrounds are open all year?"

You'll know it worked when the new answer builds on the first one and again includes numbered sources.

## Common mistakes

- **Typing only a keyword.** A word like "campgrounds" leaves Perplexity guessing what you need. *The fix:* Ask a complete question with the details that matter to you, such as the place and the time.
- **Trusting the answer without opening a source.** AI answers can contain mistakes or outdated details. *The fix:* Open at least one numbered source, especially before an important decision.
- **Reading a label as a guarantee.** Perplexity says a label is not an endorsement and doesn't rate single articles. *The fix:* Still read the source page itself.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Before you share a surprising claim or plan a trip, you can get a quick answer and open the pages behind it in the same place.
- **For your business or work:** When you prepare a short briefing, you can collect the source links along with the answer and check each one before you use it.
- **If you're just getting started:** Think of Perplexity as a research helper that shows its work. The numbered sources are the part to look at first.

## Try it now

Open [perplexity.ai](https://www.perplexity.ai), type "What are three indoor activities to do in [your city] on a rainy afternoon?" and press **Enter**. Then open one of the numbered sources and check that it matches the answer.
